one_liner: A narrow-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 1.3x fair value. Interesting below about $33.

profile.what: U.S. Bancorp is the fifth-largest US commercial bank, with a regional branch network in the West and Midwest, payments processing (Elavon) and corporate trust services.
profile.money: Net interest income from loans funded by deposits, plus fees from payments, cards, trust services and wealth management. The 2022 acquisition of MUFG Union Bank added West Coast branches.
profile.valued: Valued on P/E and price to tangible book. The multiple depends on interest margins and on rebuilding capital after rate rises cut the value of its bond holdings.
profile.peer_group: Financials · bank, insurer or asset manager

summary.sentence: A well-run regional bank with a valuable payments business.
risks: Slower growth than the largest banks.

valuation.method: Banks are valued on book value, not free cash flow. Justified price-to-book = (ROE − 3% growth) ÷ (required return − 3%), using a normalised ROE of 10.5% (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM, capped at 25%) and a required return of 11% (low) to 9% (high): 0.94–1.25 × book value per share of $42.88.

methods.name: Excess-return model on book value
methods.basis: Book value per share $42.88 × 0.94–1.25. This is how Damodaran values banks and insurers: equity is worth book value plus the returns earned above the cost of equity.
